name: Pegasus
uganda_context: Reported targeting of Ugandan journalists and officials (e.g., Canary Mugume in 2024). Discovered on devices of Ugandan activists.
details: Highly sophisticated surveillance tool capable of infiltrating smartphones (iOS/Android) without user interaction. Extracts messages, emails, media, and records calls.

name: FinFisher / FinSpy
uganda_context: Found to be used by Ugandan security agencies (CMI) under 'Operation Gladiator' between 2011-2013 to monitor opposition figures and journalists.
details: Commercial intrusion malware sold to governments. It can capture webcam video, Skype audio, passwords, and microphones.

name: Predator
uganda_context: Intellexa alliance tools have been documented targeting civil society in East Africa, presenting a regional threat.
details: Mobile spyware that typically requires the user to click a malicious link. Operates similarly to Pegasus, granting full access to device data.

name: UFED
uganda_context: Used by Ugandan police to extract data from seized devices of activists and opposition members (e.g., during 2021 elections and 2025/2026 arrests).
details: Requires physical access to the device. Bypasses lock screens and extracts all data, including encrypted messages and deleted files.

name: Safe City CCTV
uganda_context: Deployed across Kampala and major highways since 2019 under a $126M project. Linked to tracking opposition figures.
details: Network of high-definition cameras integrated with artificial intelligence and facial recognition capabilities, feeding into a centralized police command center.

name: TheTruthSpy
uganda_context: Consumer-grade spyware widely available and used in domestic contexts in Uganda, posing severe privacy risks to ordinary citizens.
details: Discreetly uploads call logs, text messages, photos, browsing history, and real-time location data to a remote server.
